question.text: Ayodhya Growth Capital AIF (Cat II) reports that its largest investee's fair value rose 45% over Q2 FY25 (from INR 200 crore to INR 290 crore). Per SEBI framework, which of the following actions is the Investment Manager REQUIRED to take?

answer.text: Inform investors with generic and specific reasons, including any changes in assumptions, projections, methodology, or accounting practices
No action; the investor PPM already discloses valuation is volatile
Reverse the valuation back to the prior quarter
Report only if fund-level NAV rose by 20%

explanation.text: The Logic: Per PDF Section 11.12: at each ASSET LEVEL, if deviation exceeds 20% between consecutive valuations or 33% in a FY, the Manager 'shall inform the investors with REASONS for the same. This information shall include both GENERIC AND SPECIFIC information, including but not limited to changes in accounting practices or policies, assumptions or projections, valuation methodology and approach, with reasons thereof.' A 45% jump between consecutive quarters breaches the 20% trigger. The Trap: PPM disclosure does not waive event-driven reporting obligations; arbitrary reversal distorts fair value; fund-level NAV threshold doesn't apply (the rule is asset-level). The disclosure trigger is absolute at asset level. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C and XIX-A test this disclosure trigger. SEBI has issued observations on Cat II funds that failed to flag asset-level deviations — this is a live inspection theme. Manager's Pro-Tip: Automate a deviation-trigger alert in your fund administrator's system: any quarterly asset mark outside 20% change should auto-generate a draft LP disclosure note, reviewed by the IC within 5 business days of the valuation date. This protects you from inadvertent non-compliance.
